I scanned the passage for trailing "not X" or "rather than X" clauses and found three candidates.

1. "Those privilege limits are imposed on purpose, rather than by accident." Purpose and accident are ordinary antonyms, so the trailer adds nothing and should be cut.

2. "Access checks default to fail-closed, rather than open." Open versus closed is the ordinary antonym of closed, so I treated this as clearly in the ordinary-knowledge category and cut it.

3. "incentivizes ethical hackers to report flaws rather than exploit them" is not a trailing clause bolted onto a finished sentence. It describes the behavior being incentivized, so I left it alone.

"Not merely an IT concern" in the conclusion is a standard "not merely X; it is Y" construction, not a trailing clause, so I left it alone.
